review-report.title: Preview Review Report
review-report.description: Coverage, known gaps, verification limits, and an unexecuted production migration plan.
review-report.body:
Preview handoff

Coverage. Verification.
Next decisions.

A transparent record of what is preserved, what is implemented, and what still requires review before any separately authorized migration.

Portfolio Preview — Delivery and Verification Report

Prepared 2026-10-12 (America/Chicago). Production repository snapshot: 5c130c816cd22a70f734b2c2ee6d6480732b1dc2.

Preview and hosting

This is an independent Sites project saved without deployment. Sites in this environment has no user-facing unpublished hosted preview. The single-file HTML is the functional offline preview; download it and open it in a browser. It includes all page views, search, filters, code, and documentation. Original external evidence links require internet access. The four gallery images are included locally. A ZIP also contains the multipage static site and source.

No live Sites URL is claimed. No production migration is performed.

Project coverage

All 13 authoritative published projects are included, each with a separate case study, source links, documentation, evidence references, troubleshooting, validation, claim limits, and next milestones. All are COMPLETE for their recorded scope. macOS remains real configuration plus simulation. Graph remains read-only delegated reporting.

  1. Windows LAPS & Advanced Group Policy — COMPLETE; projects/windows-laps-gpo; 9 rendered source documents; 18 associated public references.
  2. Microsoft Entra Hybrid Identity & Cloud Sync — COMPLETE; projects/entra-cloud-sync; 7 rendered source documents; 31 associated public references.
  3. On-Premises Microsoft Home Lab — COMPLETE; projects/on-prem-home-lab; 16 rendered source documents; 35 associated public references.
  4. Windows Admin Center Lab Management — COMPLETE; projects/windows-admin-center-lab; 16 rendered source documents; 30 associated public references.
  5. SCVMM 2022 Hyper-V Management — COMPLETE; projects/scvmm-2022; 0 rendered source documents; 7 associated public references.
  6. Azure Arc Hybrid Windows Management — COMPLETE; projects/azure-arc-hybrid-management; 0 rendered source documents; 15 associated public references.
  7. APP01 Hyper-V Storage Expansion — COMPLETE; projects/app01-storage-expansion; 0 rendered source documents; 6 associated public references.
  8. Cross-Platform Administration & Support Method — COMPLETE; projects/cross-platform-administration; 16 rendered source documents; 30 associated public references.
  9. ServiceNow Request Fulfillment & Procurement Workflow — COMPLETE; projects/servicenow-request-fulfillment; 1 rendered source documents; 1 associated public references.
  10. Microsoft 365 Messaging & Security Administration — COMPLETE; projects/m365-messaging-security; 3 rendered source documents; 17 associated public references.
  11. Windows Autopilot & Intune MDM Provisioning — COMPLETE; projects/windows-autopilot-intune; 8 rendered source documents; 15 associated public references.
  12. macOS ABM to Intune Enterprise Runbook — COMPLETE; projects/macos-abm-intune-runbook; 11 rendered source documents; 12 associated public references.
  13. Microsoft 365 Graph Administration Lab — COMPLETE; projects/m365-graph-administration-lab; 2 rendered source documents; 9 associated public references.

Source and evidence coverage

  • Read the current master registry, project index, route implementation, repository resume, and 102 Markdown source documents.
  • Inspected the recursive repository tree: 2964 entries; tree response is not truncated.
  • Rendered 98 retained technical documents as full document pages. Additional inherited supporting portfolio content is preserved under Original pages.
  • Indexed 1268 unique public artifact references. Every indexed file path was checked against the retained Git tree. This proves source existence at the commit, not current HTTP availability or independent technical execution.
  • Source-reference-only catalog records without a matching public file are retained through links to the original catalogs; no private repository is exposed or copied.
  • Scripts: 10 existing PowerShell files inspected; complete source shown alongside permissions, requirements, safety, and output descriptions. No script is executed by the site.
  • Four explicitly public-sanitized Azure Arc screenshots are included unchanged in the gallery and offline preview. They were visually inspected for the displayed technical claims and visible redactions. No screenshots are generated or altered; source links point to the pinned repository commit.
  • The original PDF resume is embedded and downloadable unchanged; the original Word file is included in the static bundle.

Implemented functionality

Responsive primary/mobile navigation; breadcrumbs; all project case studies; project search and category filters; evidence search with project/type filters and pagination; document search; expandable source documents and code; image enlargement with a native dialog; back-to-top; related projects; print styles; PDF viewing/download; external GitHub and LinkedIn links. No nonfunctional contact form or backend submission is presented.

Verification and limitations

Automated source-level QA is recorded in QA-results.json. Passed: all 159 page structures, 3,766 internal file links, all 1,268 evidence file mappings, original PDF hash preservation, JavaScript syntax, and seven filtering/pagination/escaping logic tests. Duplicate imported section IDs found during QA were corrected. No configured secret-pattern matches were found. These checks do not replace a comprehensive security audit. Browser interaction, screenshot layout review at desktop/tablet/mobile, screen-reader behavior, runtime image loading, PDF browser behavior, and Core Web Vitals are NOT TESTED because the supported browser-control skill is unavailable. No alternate browser was installed or used. Responsive CSS is implemented; that is not a claim of completed visual QA. WCAG 2.2 AA is a target, not a certification.

Missing information and unresolved gaps

  • LinkedIn could not be retrieved (HTTP 999), so no profile facts were inferred.
  • The live homepage was retrievable but its body is JavaScript-rendered; the current repository route source supplied the detailed content.
  • No independently verified credential IDs, issuer verification links, or current expiration status are available. All eleven credential names are in the repository resume. Monograms are text labels, not issuer badges.
  • No professional email is available in the current resume/contact source.
  • Windows Admin Center has distributed supporting evidence; the registry does not confirm a dedicated standalone evidence directory.
  • Cloudflare has no consolidated authoritative evidence package confirmed. Its supporting section is labeled registry-recorded operational work, with no new security assurance.
  • ServiceNow Administration & ITSM Lab is IN PROGRESS at the repository checkpoint (Phases 1–4 validated, 5–10 not started); it is not a fourteenth completed project.
  • Graph licensing assignment metadata remains discrepant even where effective licensing is validated.
  • Linux01 VLAN 30 and Proxmox VE 9.2.3 are retained repository snapshot facts, not current telemetry. Historical Cloud Sync architecture names SYNC01; no newer DC01 agent placement is asserted from chat memory.
  • The four-system restore cycle keeps Linux01/pfSense narrow PASS and WS01/DC01 INCONCLUSIVE. Separate Linux restore evidence does not replace these boundaries.
  • The full evidence collection has not received a new exhaustive visual/redaction audit; four curated gallery images were visually reviewed. Only explicitly public-sanitized images are embedded; remaining evidence is referenced at its original public source.

SEO and security

All generated static pages have unique titles/descriptions, semantic content, noindex/nofollow/noarchive, Open Graph text metadata, and canonical links to the existing production URL when an exact equivalent exists. The preview never claims the production domain as its own origin. robots.txt disallows crawling. A production sitemap is intentionally not generated for an unpublished preview; the human site map lists every created page. No tracking, third-party fonts, API credentials, submission forms, or client-side tenant access are added. Scripts are displayed, never executed. A source-level secret-pattern scan is included in QA.

Future production migration plan — NOT EXECUTED

  1. Have Jeremy review the full offline preview, every claim boundary, and the verification gaps.
  2. Complete authorized browser/accessibility/performance testing and an evidence redaction review before considering deployment.
  3. Reconcile the content with the then-current production main commit; retain all evidence, downloadable assets, and original URLs.
  4. Prepare an isolated migration branch or separate repository only after explicit authorization. Create a route mapping for all legacy URLs and a rollback snapshot.
  5. Request separate, explicit authorization for the exact production repository, deployment, domain, DNS, and Cloudflare changes. Design approval alone is not deployment authorization.
  6. Only after that authorization: set final canonical/OG URLs, generate the production sitemap, remove preview indexing blocks, retain download paths, validate links, and execute the approved deployment plan.
  7. Validate post-deployment navigation, evidence paths, TLS, caching, security headers, and redirects. Use the approved rollback plan if required.

Production protection

Every operation against the original GitHub repository and live portfolio was read-only. No original-repository commits, branches, pull requests, changes to evidence/downloads, GitHub Pages operations, domain attachment, redirect, Cloudflare DNS change, or Cloudflare security change was performed. No Cloudflare account mutation tool was used. The separate Sites source is the only Git destination written. Independent before/after Cloudflare and GitHub Pages configuration snapshots were not available, so this confirms this task's actions, not a global guarantee against unrelated external changes.
